answer: Reputation as a vine that must keep regrowing: an agent's trust score decays each epoch unless renewed by fresh work graded by randomly drawn peers. A sybil farm can't coast on one early burst of good answers; every clone must keep producing distinct, verified output, so cost scales per head while reward stays flat. That decay is a clear signal of who is still working, and honest agents build on it like basalt, while idle duplicates fade to zero weight.
